comment_box:
As a Marine Corps veteran who served two combat tours and received the Purple Heart, I am writing not only as someone who has worn the uniform, but as someone who has carried the physical and emotional weight of that service. I strongly oppose the proposed regulation published on August 4, 2025 (RIN 2900-AS31), which seeks to reinstate the exclusion of abortion services and counseling from the VA and CHAMPVA medical benefits packages under 38 CFR Part 17.

This regulation removes coverage even in cases where a veteran’s life or health is at risk, or where pregnancy results from rape or incest. That is not just a policy decision—it is a denial of care to those who have already endured trauma. I urge the VA to preserve the conditional exceptions established in 2022, which recognized the need for care in medical emergencies and situations of violence.

The justification in the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section claims that abortion services are not considered “needed” under section 1710 of title 38. But the term “needed” is not defined, and it should be interpreted through clinical judgment based on current medical standards. There are many situations where abortion care is medically warranted, and this regulation fails to account for that reality.

This exclusion will disproportionately affect veterans in rural areas and states with restrictive abortion laws, where the VA may be the only accessible provider. For many veterans, especially women and survivors of trauma, this policy would eliminate their only path to safe, necessary care.

The language stating that “scope of coverage shall exclude abortion services and abortion counseling” must be amended. Exceptions should be clearly allowed when a VA healthcare provider determines the treatment is medically necessary, especially when a veteran’s life, health, or well-being is at risk, or in cases of rape or incest.

Veterans who have served this country with honor deserve healthcare that reflects the complexity of their experiences and the reality of their needs. I respectfully urge the Department to reconsider this exclusion and uphold the VA’s mission to protect the health and dignity of every veteran and their family.
